summary: Typosquat of Tinkoff banking SDK installs site-wide.pth auto-run with DNS-TXT dead-drop resolver
details: The PyPI package 'tinkoff-cloud-apis-internal' impersonates the Russian bank Tinkoff while shipping only a trivial stub SDK. setup.py copies a telemetry.pth file into site-packages so that `import _telemetry_init` executes on every Python interpreter startup on the installer's machine, not only when this package is explicitly imported. _telemetry_init spawns a daemon thread that constructs a Client from _telemetry_transport, whose ServiceDiscovery class implements DNS TXT record lookup with segmented base64 reassembly (`_txt_lookup` returning `b64.b64decode(''.join(...))`) — a dead-drop pattern for retrieving a command/endpoint configuration from an attacker-controlled DNS zone at runtime. The current shipped configuration leaves the endpoint empty and no exec/subprocess sink is wired up, so the immediately visible bytes do not fire an outbound payload, but the persistent interpreter-wide execution hook and the DNS-based configuration channel constitute pre-positioned staging infrastructure whose behavior can be changed remotely without a new package release. The combination of banking-name impersonation,.pth-based scope broadening beyond normal import, and DNS-TXT/base64 resolver code is not consistent with any legitimate SDK function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
